reason: The bounded schedule family, generic fused-kernel reuse, serial producer-consumer ownership, and four-warp parallel ownership all fail the materiality and strict-state gates under production-relevant CUDA Graph timing.

tested_families.result: Warm best projected only 33.9 us per whole step; cache-evicted replay was 0.750x; multiwarp variants changed recurrent state.
Previously measured at 0.995621x and below the 50 us materiality floor.

tested_families.family: one program per head with four sequential BV32 slices and gated RMSNorm
tested_families.result: Bitwise exact, but CUDA Graph replay was 0.7465x because tile parallelism was serialized.

tested_families.family: one block per head with four CUDA warps and in-block gated RMSNorm
tested_families.result: CUDA Graph replay was 0.4611x; state differed at 10 BF16 elements by up to 0.00390625.

remaining_hypotheses: Fuse causal convolution into recurrence without duplicating q/k work.
Use a compiler primitive that can preserve stock BV32 tensor layout per warp while exposing a head-wide synchronization boundary.
Change recurrent-state algorithm or persistent state ownership across multiple decode steps.
reopen_conditions: A CUDA 13-compatible compiler toolchain or warp-specialized DSL becomes available and can express four stock-equivalent BV32 tiles plus an exact head-wide reduction.
A source-level design removes causal-convolution materialization and predicts at least 50 us per whole decode step without duplicated q/k computation.
The model shape, recurrent-state dtype, GPU architecture, or vLLM CUDA Graph execution contract changes.
A persistent multi-step state-owner design supplies a dependency proof and a whole-step predicted gain of at least 50 us.
claim_limit: This closes the current SM89/Qwen3.5-0.8B recurrent search budget. It is not a proof that an unknown recurrent algorithm cannot improve performance.
